parts.label: a
parts.ask: The graph of \(y = 3|x-2| + 5\) has its vertex at \(P\). Find the coordinates of \(P\).
parts.method: Vertex where the modulus is zero

parts.label: b
parts.method: Solve each branch, then check it

steps.why: Each branch only holds on its own side of \(x = 2\).
\(\tfrac{17}{7} = 2.43\ldots \geq 2\): on this branch, so keep it.
\(5\) is not less than \(2\): reject it.

parts.label: c
parts.ask: The line \(y = kx + 4\) meets \(y = 3|x-2| + 5\) at 2 distinct points. Find the range of values of \(k\).

steps.text: Every line \(y = kx + 4\) passes through \((0, 4)\), below the V. It meets the V twice when it passes above \(P\) and crosses the right branch.

steps.why: At \(k = \tfrac{1}{2}\) it meets the V only at \(P\), so \(k > \tfrac{1}{2}\).

steps.text: The right branch has gradient 3. If \(k \geq 3\), the line never catches it, so \(k < 3\).
steps.why: This upper limit is the one most people miss.
